372742.title: The sharp linear Turán bound conjecture for 4-edge linear paths
372742.literal_statement:
Let $P_4^r$ be the $r$-uniform linear path with four edges, and let $ex_r^{\mathrm{lin}}(n,P_4^r)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex linear $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $P_4^r$. A Steiner system $S(2,r,r^2)$ is a design on $r^2$ vertices in which every pair of vertices lies in exactly one $r$-element block. **The sharp bound conjecture.**

$$
ex_r^{\mathrm{lin}}(n,P_4^r) \leq \dfrac{(r+1)n}{r}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if the linear $r$-uniform hypergraph is the union of disjoint Steiner systems $S(2,r,r^2)$, given that the Steiner system $S(2,r,r^2)$ exists.

This conjecture would make the lower bound obtained from disjoint copies of $S(2,r,r^2)$ sharp and would characterize all equality cases when the relevant Steiner system exists. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

359786.title: Strengthened Chen–Lih–Wu and Kostochka–Pelsmajer–West conjecture
359786.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an $r$-colorable graph, with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\leq r$. Let an $r$-list assignment $L$ assign $r$ available colors to each vertex, and call $G$ **equitably $r$-choosable** if every such assignment has a proper list coloring using each color at most $\left\lceil |V(G)|/r\right\rceil$ times. A coloring is **SE $r$-choosable** when it satisfies the stronger size condition defined in the paper: all color classes have size at most $\left\lceil |V(G)|/r\right\rceil$, with at most $|V(G)|\mathbin{\operatorname{mod}^*}r$ classes attaining that upper bound. **Strengthened conjecture.** Either $r$ is odd and $K_{r,r}\subseteq G$, or $G$ is equitably $r$-choosable and even SE $r$-choosable. The statement is proposed in the concluding remarks as a possible strengthening; it is not claimed to be proved, and its status is open.

366628.title: Negative type conjecture for 3-subdivisions of graphs with a $K_{2,3}$ minor
366628.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph containing $K_{2,3}$ as a minor, and let the $3$-subdivision of $G$ be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of $G$ three times. Equip it with its shortest path metric.

**Negative type conjecture.** There is no graph $G$ with a $K_{2,3}$ minor where the shortest distance metric of the $3$-subdivision of $G$ has negative type.

This conjecture proposes that the obstruction to negative type established for sufficiently fine subdivisions already occurs for the $3$-subdivision. The preceding results give a bound of $180$ and show that the $2$-subdivision of $K_4$ is even $\ell_1$-embeddable, leaving the sharp threshold between these cases open.

368236.title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture for edge sum-labellings
368236.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. For a positive integer $k$, an edge $k$-labelling is a map $\ell:E(G)\to\{1,\dots,k\}$. For each vertex $u$, define its incident sum by

$$
\sigma_\ell(u)=\sum_{v\in N(u)}\ell(uv).
$$

The labelling is sum-proper when adjacent vertices have distinct incident sums, and $\chi^e_{\rm S}(G)$ is the least such $k$, when it exists. **The 1-2-3 Conjecture.** If $G$ is connected and $G\neq K_2$, then

$$
\chi^e_{\rm S}(G)\leq 3.
$$

The conjecture was raised by Karoński, Łuczak, and Thomason in 2004 and was recently solved by Keusch, so its database status is solved.

371731.title: Nýdl's reconstructibility conjecture for trees
371731.literal_statement: For an $n$-vertex graph, the $m$-deck is the multiset of its unlabeled induced $m$-vertex subgraphs, and a family of graphs is **weakly $celltext{ell}$-reconstructible** if no two graphs in the family have the same $(n-celltext{ell})$-deck. **Nýdl's conjecture.** For $ncellge 2celltext{ell}+1$, no two $n$-vertex trees have the same $(n-celltext{ell})$-deck; equivalently, trees with at least $2celltext{ell}+1$ vertices are weakly $celltext{ell}$-reconstructible. The conjecture is refuted by two $13$-vertex trees with the same $7$-deck, although the stated bound is sharp in general because examples with $2celltext{ell}$ vertices and the same $celltext{ell}$-deck are known.

359435.title: Modified reconstruction conjecture for trees beyond the known exceptions
359435.literal_statement:
For an $n$-vertex tree, its $(n-\ell)$-deck is the multiset of induced subgraphs obtained by deleting $\ell$ vertices. A tree is **$\ell$-reconstructible** if it is determined up to isomorphism by its $(n-\ell)$-deck.

**Modified tree reconstruction conjecture.** For $n\ge 2\ell+1$, except when $(n,\ell)\in\{(5,2),(13,6)\}$, every $n$-vertex tree is $\ell$-reconstructible. The threshold on $n$ is known to be sharp.

This modifies Nýdl's conjecture by excluding the known five-vertex and thirteen-vertex exceptions. The source presents the statement as a conjectural modification; the supplied parser gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

360350.title: The explicit connectivity conjecture for breadth-critical tangles
360350.literal_statement: Define a sequence of non-negative integers by $t_0=0$ and $t_i=3t_{i-1}+1$ for $i\geq 1$, equivalently $t_i=(3^i-1)/2$. Let $M$ be a matroid with a breadth-critical tangle $\mathcal{T}$ of order at least $k$. A matroid is **$(t_0,t_1,\ldots,t_{k-2})$-connected** if, whenever $F\subseteq E(M)$ has $\lambda(F)=i$ for $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,k-2\}$, either $|F|\leq t_i$ or $|E(M)-F|\leq t_i$. **The explicit connectivity conjecture.** If $\mathcal{T}$ is a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ in $M$, then $M$ is $(t_0,t_1,\ldots,t_{k-2})$-connected. This is presented as a stronger version of the bounded connectivity conjecture, motivated by the bound $13=(3\times4)+1$ for $4$-separating sets in weakly $4$-connected matroids; it remains open.

382182.title: Optimal Power of Few conjecture for majority dynamics
382182.literal_statement:
Let $G(n,p)$ be an Erdős–Rényi random graph, let $\Delta$ denote Red's initial advantage, and let $p$ satisfy

$$
p \ge (1 + \lambda)(\log n)/n.
$$

**Optimal Power of Few conjecture.** There is a function $f(x)$ such that $f(x)>1/2$ for $x>0$, $f(x)$ tends to $1$ as $x$ tends to infinity, and, in majority dynamics on $G(n,p)$ with initial advantage $\Delta$ for Red, Red wins with probability

$$
f(\Delta\sqrt{p}).
$$

This formalizes the claim that an initial advantage of order $p^{-1/2}$ is sufficient for Red to win with probability bounded away from $1/2$ and that the winning probability approaches $1$ as the scaled advantage grows. A result of Sah and Sawhney, improving work of Devlin and Berkowitz, confirms the conjecture when $p$ tends to zero sufficiently slowly, namely when $p\ge (\log n)^{-1/16}$; the general case remains open.

372614.title: Jain's $S^2$-map conjecture
372614.literal_statement:
Let $S^2$ be the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$. **Jain's $S^2$-map conjecture.** There exists a map

$$
\varphi:S^2 \rightarrow \{-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4\}
$$

such that antipodal points of $S^2$ receive opposite values and the three vertices of every inscribed equilateral triangle on a great circle have images whose sum is zero. The source presents this as one of two conjectures implying Tutte's $5$-flow conjecture; no resolution is given.

372883.title: Non-well-quasi-ordering of k-connected bipartite graphs by bipartite minors
372883.literal_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, and consider the class of $k$-connected bipartite graphs with the bipartite minor relation. **Bipartite-minor non-well-quasi-order conjecture.** There exists no $k$ such that the class of $k$-connected bipartite graphs is well-quasi-ordered by the bipartite minor relation. This conjecture extends the proved failure of well-quasi-ordering for $2$-connected bipartite graphs, asserting that increasing the connectivity requirement never yields a well-quasi-order.

373575.title: The four-cycle conjecture for genus-one configuration curves
373575.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a 1-dof graph, meaning a graph whose generic configuration fiber has one degree of freedom, and let its generic fiber have genus one. A graph is said to be equivalent to a four-cycle when it has exactly four maximal rigid subgraphs attached in a cycle. **Four-cycle conjecture.** Then $G$ has four maximal rigid subgraphs and is equivalent to a four-cycle. This would classify the graphs whose generic configuration fiber has genus one, extending the paper's classification of graphs with genus-zero generic fiber. The claim is motivated by small experiments and is presented as a natural next step, so it remains open.

373624.title: Erdős–Sárközy–Stewart quadratic prime-factor conjecture for subset sums
373624.literal_statement:
For a finite set $A\ne\textstyle\varnothing$ of positive integers, let $\Sigma^*(A)$ denote the set of nonempty subset sums, and let $P(A)$ be the greatest prime factor of $\prod_{a\in A}a$. **Erdős–Sárközy–Stewart's quadratic conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
P(\Sigma^*(A))>c|A|^2.
$$

This is a quantitative strengthening of the preceding prime-factor growth conjecture and is presented by the source as the second conjecture of Erdős, Sárközy, and Stewart.

374217.title: The 1-2-3 conjecture for locally finite polygonal tilings
374217.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite tiling with a finite number of polygonal prototiles. Suppose

$$
\mathcal T=\bigcupdot_{k=1}^N(\varLambda_k+\mathcal P_k)
$$

is a partition into translations of finitely many, not necessarily distinct, finite subgraphs, and let

$$
l_k:\mathcal P_k\to\{1,2,3\}
$$

be edge-weightings. **The 1-2-3 conjecture for locally finite polygonal tilings.** There exist such a partition and weightings $l_k$ that produce a global solution to the 1-2-3 problem, meaning that the resulting weighted degrees of adjacent vertices are different. This conjecture gives a more nuanced patch-based formulation after purely locally derivable solutions are shown not to exist for some tilings; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.

374559.title: The strong odd Hadwiger-type conjecture for clique immersions
374559.literal_statement:
Let $t\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ and let $G$ be a graph. An immersion of $K_t$ is **strong odd** if its paths are pairwise edge-disjoint, have odd length, and no terminal is an interior vertex of a path. **Strong odd immersion coloring conjecture.** If $G$ has no strong odd $K_t$-immersion, then

$$
\chi(G)<t.
$$
 This conjecture extends clique-immersion coloring conjectures by imposing both the strong and odd conditions. It is known for $t\leq 4$ and for several special graph classes, while the general statement remains open; the paper's main theorem gives a bound when $\alpha(G)\leq 2$.

374559.ordinary_attempt_and_gap: Actual source Conjecture 1 remains general; Theorem 1 assumes alpha<=2 and has factor 3/2. Removing that hypothesis or replacing the factor by one is unproved. A disproof of the odd-minor Hadwiger conjecture does not automatically refute odd immersions, whose paths may share internal vertices. Conflicting literal solved metadata is not proof.
